clue.text: Leave kid some meat

parts.note: to leave someone unharmed is to spare them
to kid is to tease, which is also to rib

explanation.surface: An instruction to let a young goat go free, or to leave it some food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' and 'kid' both look like nouns or plain verbs about goats; each is a synonym piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare rib is a cut of pork ribs, so it is one kind of meat.

clue.text: Clarify golf fair hosts

indicators.note: hosts means the word for fair holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: fair in the sense of clean or unblemished, so pure
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Explaining which golf fair is staging the event.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge a liquid is to clear it of impurities, an old sense of clarify.

clue.text: Unfortunate upset: the Spanish pummel Germany

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means the whole string is turned upside down

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
to pummel is to beat repeatedly, or batter

explanation.surface: A sorry episode in which Spaniards trounce the Germans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like part of the definition but turns ELBATTERGER upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Regrettable means deserving regret, so unlucky or unfortunate.

clue.text: Gets back about one to tuck into seafood

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: to tuck into means to place the letter inside the word for seafood

parts.note: clams are shellfish eaten as seafood
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone eating seafood regains their strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' suggests eating, but it puts I inside CLAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover or retrieve it, which is to get it back.

clue.text: Dominant suspect divides support one held in court

indicators.note: divides means the scrambled letters split the word for support

parts.note: a bracket is a support fixed to a wall to hold a shelf

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or unreliable, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shady dominant figure undermining backing for someone in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' shuffles DOMINANT, and 'divides' splits the word for support around it. 'court' suggests law but means a sports court.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the racket a player grips on a badminton court.

clue.text: Make good soldiers revolt

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British Army
a coup is a sudden uprising against a government

explanation.surface: An order for troops to rise up and set things right.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup a loss is to make it good by recovering the amount.

clue.text: Top crumpled, getting pressed

indicators.note: Top tells us to remove the leading letter of the word for crumpled

parts.note: crumpled means squashed, or crushed

explanation.surface: A shirt or blouse came out creased after ironing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a garment but tells us to drop the C at the top of CRUSHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed for time means hurried, which is rushed.

clue.text: Short, short dog

indicators.note: the second short says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: short in manner means curt

explanation.surface: A terse description of a small dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel or snappish dog.

clue.text: Dodgy tune in car played

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A questionable song heard on the car radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' looks like it describes the tune, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgy can mean unreliable or doubtful, which is uncertain.

clue.text: Awful time with smoke around

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for a smoke the other way round

parts.note: a cigar is something one smokes, so a smoke

explanation.surface: A grim moment spent amid clouds of smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoke' looks like a verb or haze, but it is a noun for something smoked, which 'around' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tragic is dreadful or calamitous, a stronger sense of awful.

clue.text: Shame having gas with cider drunk

indicators.note: something drunk is in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The embarrassment of getting wind after downing cider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like it belongs with the cider, but it signals that GAS and CIDER are mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A disgrace is a loss of honour or respect, which is what shame means as a noun.

clue.text: Turn over broadcast of player in tournament

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is spoken out, so we use its sound

parts.note: a seed is a ranked player placed in a tennis or similar tournament draw

explanation.surface: Handing over coverage rights for a competitor in a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals that SEED is said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn over territory or rights is to surrender them, which is to cede them.

clue.text: Fruit in an assorted tray of food

indicators.note: in shows the fruit sits inside the little word an

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so the letters of tray are rearranged

explanation.surface: A citrus fruit placed in a mixed tray of snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an assorted tray' reads as one phrase, but 'an' belongs with the fruit; 'assorted' rearranges TRAY into TARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimentary describes things relating to nourishment or digestion, as in the alimentary canal.

clue.text: Having had a few triumphs capturing king for game

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, having had a few drinks

indicators.note: capturing means the word for triumphs takes in the letter

parts.note: triumphs are wins
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A tipsy player wins several times by taking the king in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing king' suggests chess; it puts K inside WINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddlywinks is a children's game of flicking small discs into a cup.

clue.text: Dislike Italian with charm

parts.note: con is the Italian word for with
to charm someone is to lure or tempt them

explanation.surface: Finding an Italian with charm disagreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian with' looks like a description of a charming Italian; it asks for the Italian word for 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is scorn or disdain, a strong dislike for someone or something.

clue.text: This compiler's inferior to old guns, it's apparent

indicators.note: inferior to means placed below, which in a down entry puts this piece after the rest

parts.note: Stens are British submachine guns of the Second World War
the setter saying this compiler has, or I have, shortened to I've

explanation.surface: A crossword setter confessing to being no match for veteran gunners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inferior to' puts IVE beneath O + STENS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensive means showing or seeming, close to ostensible, so outwardly evident.

clue.text: Agreement from chief to switch banks

indicators.note: banks are the two sides, so the end letters of the word for chief change places

parts.note: the lead is the principal or chief role

explanation.surface: A deal struck when the boss moves money between banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to switch banks' swaps the first and last letters of LEAD, its two edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal is an arrangement or bargain reached between parties.

clue.text: Happen upon ruminant consuming hot sauce

indicators.note: upon means sitting on top of the rest in this down entry

parts.note: to be in the sense of to take place, or happen

indicators.note: consuming means the animal takes the letter inside it

parts.note: a camel is a cud-chewing ruminant
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Coming across a camel eating something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upon' puts BE above CHAMEL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Béchamel is a classic white sauce made with milk, butter and flour.

clue.text: Little bit pig-headed, born to lose

indicators.note: to lose means the word for born is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: pig-headed means obstinate, or stubborn

explanation.surface: Someone a little obstinate, apparently destined to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is a short remaining piece, such as of a pencil or ticket, so a small bit.

clue.text: Irritating rogue in legend

indicators.note: rogue means behaving out of line, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troublesome scoundrel appearing in an old story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' looks like a noun for the villain; it signals rearranging IN LEGEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Needling means provoking or annoying someone with persistent jibes.

clue.text: Rat where hare might be

definitions.meaning: to rat on someone is to tell tales to the authorities
a hare's nest is called its form, so a resting hare is in its form

explanation.definitionFit: To inform is to betray secrets, as a rat does; split, the letters say a hare sits in its form.

clue.text: Below ground, erne at high shelters

indicators.note: shelters means the phrase holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: A sea eagle flying high finds cover lower down.
explanation.walkthrough: An erne is a sea eagle. 'shelters' says the letters run inside 'ground, erne at high'.
explanation.definitionFit: Underneath and below both mean at a lower level than something.

clue.text: Poor tip of small change gets disregarded

indicators.note: tip of points to the opening letter of the word for small change
gets disregarded means that opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a tweak is a slight adjustment

explanation.surface: A meagre gratuity in coins goes ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small change' looks like coins but means TWEAK; 'tip of' and 'gets disregarded' remove its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor as in feeble or inadequate, a sense shared with weak.

clue.text: Regularly seen fairies near ring

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the following words

explanation.surface: Fairies are often found near a fairy ring.
explanation.walkthrough: A fairy ring is a circle of mushrooms, which the surface leans on; 'ring' here is a boxing or circus ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space for contests or shows, like a boxing ring.

clue.text: Charge pirate in cutter

parts.note: a bill is a charge for goods or services
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: Accusing a buccaneer aboard a small sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' suggests the boat, which suits the pirate, but here it is a cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A billhook is a curved-bladed tool for cutting branches and hedges.

clue.text: Cover opening in Lyceum with mounted policeman

indicators.note: opening in means the first letter of the theatre's name
mounted means raised up, so in a down entry the letters run upwards

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector

explanation.surface: Covering a theatre premiere with a policeman on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted policeman' suggests a horseback officer; it is DI turned upwards. The Lyceum is a London theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A lid is the cover on top of a box or pot.

clue.text: Some time after ditching university, daughter becomes rich

indicators.note: after ditching means the letter for university is removed

parts.note: a minute is a short span of time
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A daughter who quits college and makes her fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Minted is British slang for very wealthy, as if one owned the mint.

clue.text: Diggers returned carrying diamonds rarely

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed word holds another letter
returned means the word for diggers is read backwards

parts.note: moles are burrowing animals, natural diggers
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Miners coming back with gems is a rare event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diggers' suggests miners, but they are MOLES; 'returned' makes SELOM, and 'carrying' puts D within.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom means not often, the same as rarely.

clue.text: Dutch explorer circling large island that may provide fortune

indicators.note: circling means the explorer's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Abel Tasman was the Dutch navigator who reached Tasmania and New Zealand
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A Dutch voyager sailing round a big island in search of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is a charm believed to bring good luck to its owner.
